description: A pharmacy director must decide whether to approve a non-formulary outpatient medication for a patient expected to leave the hospital tomorrow and finalize the medication's authorization, packaging, and teaching plan, with input from infectious disease, utilization review, and discharge nursing.

shared_context.S1: A medically stable patient is expected to leave the hospital tomorrow with an outpatient treatment plan.
shared_context.S2: The treating team has requested a formulary exception for oral fidaxomicin because the medication is not routinely stocked for discharge prescriptions.
shared_context.S3: Marisol has final authority to approve or deny the formulary exception and its associated dispensing plan.
shared_context.S4: Hospital policy calls for a medication-exception huddle with infectious disease, utilization review, and discharge nursing before the pharmacy director signs the final plan.
shared_context.S5: For the huddle record, each participating department states its relevant clinical, authorization, or patient-use recommendation aloud before Marisol finalizes the plan; an unclear report is repeated and clarified before sign-off.

PF1.text: The patient has had a second confirmed episode in six months, so infectious-disease guidance supports fidaxomicin 200 mg by mouth twice daily for exactly 10 days rather than the routine alternative; Dr. Chen reviewed the result this morning, but the updated recommendation is not yet in the discharge note.

PF2.text: The payer approved fidaxomicin for this patient for exactly 10 days under authorization code FDX-6382, provided the hospital dispenses it before discharge; Ravi received the approval notice directly and has not entered it into the utilization system yet.

PF3.text: The patient lives alone and cannot reliably open a standard child-resistant bottle, so discharge nursing has arranged a unit-dose blister pack and a medication-teaching visit at exactly 16:30 tomorrow; Lena confirmed both details with the patient today, but they are not yet on the discharge task list.

acceptance_conditions: The formulary exception must be approved for fidaxomicin.
The prescription must specify 200 mg by mouth twice daily for exactly 10 days.
The clinical plan must reflect the second confirmed episode in six months and the infectious-disease recommendation for fidaxomicin.
The authorization must be recorded as approved under code FDX-6382.
The medication must be dispensed in a unit-dose blister pack.
A medication-teaching visit at exactly 16:30 tomorrow must be committed and recorded in the teaching visit field.
The recurrent-episode finding must be cited as justification for the medication approval.

content_checks.C1: decisions['formulary_exception_approved'] == True and decisions['medication'] in ['fidaxomicin', 'oral fidaxomicin']
content_checks.C2: decisions['dose_mg'] == 200 and ('twice daily' in decisions['frequency'] or 'BID' in decisions['frequency'] or 'bid' in decisions['frequency']) and decisions['course_days'] == 10
content_checks.C3: ('second confirmed' in decisions['clinical_justification'] or 'Second confirmed' in decisions['clinical_justification']) and ('six months' in decisions['clinical_justification'] or 'six-month' in decisions['clinical_justification']) and 'fidaxomicin' in decisions['clinical_justification'] and decisions['dose_mg'] == 200 and decisions['course_days'] == 10 and ('twice daily' in decisions['frequency'] or 'BID' in decisions['frequency'] or 'bid' in decisions['frequency'])
content_checks.C4: ('approved' in decisions['authorization_status'] or 'authorized' in decisions['authorization_status'] or 'Approved' in decisions['authorization_status'] or 'Authorized' in decisions['authorization_status']) and decisions['authorization_code'] == 'FDX-6382'
content_checks.C5: decisions['packaging'] in ['unit-dose blister pack', 'Unit-dose blister pack']
content_checks.C6: '16:30' in decisions['teaching_visit_time'] and any(('teaching' in c['detail'] or '16:30' in c['detail']) and ('Lena' in c['target'] or 'discharge' in c['target'] or 'patient' in c['target'] or 'nursing' in c['target']) for c in commitments)

provenance_checks.P1: 'PF1' in credited_facts and 'PF1' in justification_fact_ids and 'PF1' in revealed

decisive_facts.why: The second confirmed episode changes the medication choice to fidaxomicin, fixes the prescription at 200 mg twice daily by mouth for exactly 10 days, and supplies the recurrent-episode and infectious-disease justification text.
The payer notice changes the authorization fields from unresolved to an approved status with the exact code FDX-6382.

The patient's inability to open a standard bottle changes the packaging to a unit-dose blister pack, and the confirmed nursing arrangement fixes the teaching visit at 16:30 tomorrow and requires it to be included in the discharge task plan.
